chapter: Jazz opinions, Jelly Roll and the Rhythm Club
title: Was Jelly Roll telling the truth
summary: He says Morton told jokes and nearly everything he said came out right.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: There was a question as to some of the things I've read and heard from other people that Jelly Roll wasn't always telling the truth. I heard statements - they said that he would have - he told everybody that he wrote everything, that he was responsible for every solo that everybody played and that he started jazz and the whole thing. Is that true?

Let me tell you one thing. It's funny, Jelly Roll Morton used to tell jokes, you know. He said it take about 25 niggers to make a chinch. He said niggers ain't no good. Yes, he said it, and the musicians don't forget it today. He didn't lie much. He said it'd take 25 niggers to make a chinch. (LAUGHTER) He said it, he said that.
Why would he say something like that?
He had that diamond tooth up there. He didn't care, and he was talking and pretty near everything he said it came out pretty near right.
